description: sqrt(2)*sqrt(3) = sqrt(6) is mathematically true. THE HEADLINE FINDING (confirmed empirically, not just predicted): equal() does not decline here -- it returns ZeroTest::Certified{equal:false}, a CONFIDENT, CERTIFIED, WRONG claim that two equal real numbers differ. Printing the certificate's own witness ({:?}) shows exactly why: the zero-test's atom algebra treats sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(6) as three independent atoms named \0sqrt:2, \0sqrt:3, \0sqrt:6, so the witness polynomial is the genuinely-nonzero free-algebra expression 1*(sqrt:2)*(sqrt:3) - 1*(sqrt:6). The certificate is internally consistent (that free-algebra polynomial really is nonzero and re-derivable) but its scope is narrower than real-number equality, and the ZeroTest::Certified label does not say so. OWNERSHIP: the fix is lane cas-witness's, tracked as file 13 item 1 wave two -- this corpus excludes known_defect entries from its agree/disagree/decline tally so the aggregate gate does not redden for every session while that fix is in flight, but the harness asserts the disagreement PERSISTS and exits nonzero the moment it does not, forcing this entry's tier back to core once the fix lands

observed_wrong_answer.note: ZeroTest::Certified{equal:false}, confirmed by printing the witness

justification: sympy: sp.simplify(sp.sqrt(2)*sp.sqrt(3)-sp.sqrt(6)) == 0, confirming the identity is true. This is exactly the class of defect CLAUDE.md's evidence-and-checker-discipline section describes: a certificate whose label (Certified) outruns what it actually establishes
